   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="tpb:MasterSettlementAgreementMsaPolicyTextBlock" id="c141079635" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Master Settlement Agreement (MSA)</b>&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Forty-<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078739">six</span> states, certain U.S. territories, and the District of Columbia are parties to the Master Settlement Agreement (&#8220;MSA&#8221;) and the Smokeless Tobacco Master Settlement Agreement (&#8220;STMSA&#8221;). To the Company&#8217;s knowledge, signatories to the MSA include <ix:nonFraction id="c141078740" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:NumberOfCigaretteManufacturersAndOrDistributorsThatSignedAgreement" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">49</ix:nonFraction> cigarette manufacturers and/or distributors. The only signatory to the STMSA is US Smokeless Tobacco Company. In the Company&#8217;s opinion, the fundamental basis for each agreement is the states&#8217; consents to withdraw all claims for monetary, equitable, and injunctive relief against certain tobacco products manufacturers and others and, in return, the signatories have agreed to certain marketing restrictions and regulations as well as certain payment obligations.</p> <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pursuant to the MSA and subsequent states&#8217; statutes, a &#8220;cigarette manufacturer&#8221; (which is defined to also include make-your-own ("MYO") cigarette tobacco) has the option of either becoming a signatory to the MSA or opening, funding, and maintaining an escrow account, with sub-accounts on behalf of each settling state. The STMSA has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> similar provisions. The MSA escrow accounts are governed by states&#8217; statutes that expressly give the manufacturers the option of opening, funding, and maintaining an escrow account in lieu of becoming a signatory to the MSA. The statutes require companies who are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> signatories to the MSA to deposit, on an annual basis, into qualified banks, escrow funds based on the number of cigarettes or cigarette equivalents, i.e., the pounds of MYO tobacco, sold. The purpose of these statutes is expressly stated to be to eliminate the cost disadvantage the settling manufacturers have as a result of entering into the MSA. Such companies are entitled to direct the investment of the escrowed funds and withdraw any appreciation, but cannot withdraw the principal for <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078743">25</span> years from the year of each annual deposit, except to withdraw funds deposited pursuant to an individual state&#8217;s escrow statute to pay a final judgment to that state&#8217;s plaintiffs in the event of such a final judgment against the company. Either option &#8211; becoming an MSA signatory or establishing an escrow account &#8211; is permissible.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company chose to open and fund an MSA escrow account as its means of compliance. It is management&#8217;s opinion, due to the possibility of future federal or state regulations, though <em style="font: inherit;">none</em> have to date been enacted, that entering into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or both of the settlement agreements or establishing and maintaining an escrow account would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily prevent future regulations from having a material adverse effect on the results of operations, financial position, and cash flows of the Company.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Various states have enacted or proposed complementary legislation intended to curb the activity of certain manufacturers and importers of cigarettes that are selling into MSA states without signing the MSA or who have failed to properly establish and fund a qualifying escrow account. To the best of the Company&#8217;s knowledge, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> such statute has been enacted which could inadvertently and negatively impact the Company, which has been, and is currently, fully compliant with all applicable laws, regulations, and statutes. However, there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that the enactment of any such complementary legislation in the future will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on the results of operations, financial position, or cash flows of the Company.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Pursuant to the MSA escrow account statutes, in order to be compliant with the MSA escrow requirements, companies selling products covered by the MSA are required to deposit such funds for each calendar year into a qualifying escrow account by <em style="font: inherit;"> April 15 </em>of the following year. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company had on deposit approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078750" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">32.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, the fair value of which was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078751" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DepositAssetsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">29.9</ix:nonFraction> million. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company had on deposit approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078752" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DepositAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">32.1</ix:nonFraction> million, the fair value of which was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078753" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DepositAssetsFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">28.7</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;During <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> monies were deposited into this qualifying escrow account. The investment vehicles available to the Company are specified in the state escrow agreements and are limited to low-risk government securities.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company discontinued its generic category of MYO in <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> and its<i> </i>Zig-Zag<i><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;"> </sup></i>branded MYO cigarette smoking tobacco in <em style="font: inherit;">2017.</em> Thus, pending a change in MSA legislation, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining product lines covered by the MSA and will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be required to make future escrow deposits.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has chosen to invest a portion of the MSA escrow, from time to time, in U.S. Government securities including Treasury inflation-protected securities, Treasury notes&#160;and Treasury bonds. These investments are classified as available-for-sale and carried at fair value. Realized losses are prohibited under the MSA; thus, any investment with an unrealized loss position will be held until the value is recovered, or until maturity.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
    <ix:exclude>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" id="c141079636" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Concentration of Credit Risk:</b><i> </i>At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company had bank deposits, including MSA escrow accounts, in excess of federally insured limits of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078763" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashUninsuredAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">221.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078764" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CashUninsuredAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">47.4</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. During <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company invested a portion of the MSA escrow accounts in U.S. Government securities including TIPS, Treasury notes, and Treasury bonds.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company sells its products to distributors, retail establishments, and consumers throughout the U.S. and also sells <i>Zig-Zag</i>&#174; premium cigarette papers in Canada and some smaller quantities in other countries. For <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078768">not</span> have any customers that accounted for more than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of net sales. There was <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078770">one</span> customer&#160;that accounted for more than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of net sales for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and there were <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078773">no</span> customers that accounted for more than <em style="font: inherit;">10%</em> of nets sales for&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>. The Company performs periodic credit evaluations of its customers and generally does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> require collateral on trade receivables. Historically, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> experienced significant credit losses.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141079638" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i></p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Recently adopted</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued guidance&#160;which enhances income tax disclosures to require reporting entities to disclose annual income taxes paid, net of refunds, disaggregated by federal, state, and foreign taxes and to provide additional disaggregated information for individual jurisdictions under certain conditions. The guidance also requires disclosure of amounts&#160;and&#160;percentages in the annual rate reconciliation table, rather than amounts&#160;or&#160;percentages, and will eliminate certain existing disclosure requirements related to uncertain tax positions and unrecognized deferred tax liabilities. The Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> prospectively in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> See Note <em style="font: inherit;">15</em> "Income Taxes" for new disclosures relating to <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> only.</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Issued but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet adopted</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued guidance requiring reporting entities to disclose in the notes to the financial statements, specified information about certain categories of expenses including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation and amortization for each caption&#160;on the income statement where such expenses are included.&#160;This guidance will be effective for the Company beginning with its fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> annual financial statements and interim periods thereafter. Early adoption is permitted, in addition to either prospective or retrospective application. The Company is currently assessing the impact and extent to which this guidance will affect its disclosures.&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> Assets and Liabilities&#160;Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations</b>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company entered into an&#160;agreement to contribute&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141078790" contextRef="i_2025-01-02_OwnershipAxis-SouthBeachBrandsLlcMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:PercentageOfSubsidiaryContributedByParentToJointVenture" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of its interest in SBB, the subsidiary that owns and operates the Company&#8217;s&#160;CDS&#160;segment, to GWO&#160;in exchange for <ix:nonFraction id="c141078791" contextRef="i_2025-01-02_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-GeneralWirelessOperationsIncMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">49</ix:nonFraction>% of the issued and outstanding GWO common stock&#160;on a fully-diluted basis. GWO is majority owned by Standard General, LP.&#160;Under certain circumstances the Company has the right to redeem the contribution of SBB from GWO at fair market value. In addition, the Company received an option with a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-02_2025-01-02_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-GeneralWirelessOperationsIncMember" name="tpb:EquityMethodInvestmentOptionToPurchaseInterestPeriod" id="c141078792" format="ixt-sec:duryear">15</ix:nonNumeric>-year term to purchase the remaining <ix:nonFraction id="c141078793" contextRef="i_2025-01-02_LegalEntityAxis-StandardGeneralLpMember_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-GeneralWirelessOperationsIncMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EquityMethodInvestmentOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">51</ix:nonFraction>% of GWO at an exercise price initially set at $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078794" contextRef="i_2025-01-02_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-GeneralWirelessOperationsIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:EquityMethodInvestmentOptionPrice" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">22.0</ix:nonFraction> million, which decreases over time based on certain tax sharing payments to GWO.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The assets and liabilities associated with the CDS business have been classified as held for sale as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024,&#160;</em>and its financial results are classified as discontinued operations and reported separately for all periods presented herein. With the strategic shift of the Company's operations, as a result of this transaction, the CDS segment has been classified as discontinued operations. As a result, the Company now has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078795">two</span> reportable segments as disclosed in Note <em style="font: inherit;">21,</em> "Segment Information".&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Upon meeting the criteria for&#160;held&#160;for&#160;sale&#160;classification, the Company recorded a non-cash charge&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078797" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-CreativeDistributionSolutionsProductsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DisposalGroupNotDiscontinuedOperationLossGainOnWriteDown" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">8.8</ix:nonFraction> million with an equivalent valuation allowance against net assets held for sale to reduce the carrying value of the disposal group to fair value.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2024, </em>a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company invested $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078802" contextRef="d_2024-09-01_2024-09-30_OwnershipAxis-AlpSupplyCoLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireInterestInJointVenture" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction> million to acquire a <ix:nonFraction id="c141078803" contextRef="d_2024-09-01_2024-09-30_OwnershipAxis-AlpSupplyCoLlcMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:VariableInterestEntityOwnershipPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% ownership interest in ALP Supply Co., LLC ("ALP").&#160;Additionally, the Company has provided ALP with a $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078804" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_OwnershipAxis-AlpSupplyCoLlcMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCredit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">10.0</ix:nonFraction> million line of credit.&#160;ALP is a joint venture established between the subsidiary and Last Country Ventures, LLC for the purpose of selling and distributing tobacco-free moist nicotine pouches in various strengths.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em> Derivative Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Foreign Currency</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s policy is to manage the risks associated with foreign exchange rate movements. The policy allows hedging up to <ix:nonFraction id="c141078818" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:PercentageOfAnticipatedPurchasesOfInventoryThatMayBeHedgedUnderInventoryContracts" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of its anticipated purchases of inventory over a forward period that will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exceed <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:DerivativeTermOfContract" id="c141078820" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> rolling and consecutive months. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>from time to time, hedge currency for non-inventory purchases, e.g., production equipment, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to exceed <ix:nonFraction id="c141078822" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:PercentageOfPurchasePriceOfNoninventoryPurchasesThatMayBeHedged" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the purchase price. During <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, the Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> execute any foreign currency contracts. During&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Company executed various foreign exchange contracts which met hedge accounting requirements for the purchase of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078826">&#8364;3.6</span>&#160;million and sale of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078827">&#8364;3.6</span>&#160;million.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company had <ix:nonFraction id="c141078828" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember_PositionAxis-LongMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> foreign currency contracts outstanding.&#160;&#160;At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company had foreign currency contracts outstanding for the purchase of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078829">&#8364;2.1</span> million and sale of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078830">&#8364;2.1</span> million. The fair value of the foreign currency contracts at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>resulted in an asset of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078831" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction> million included in Other current assets and a liability of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078832" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million included in Accrued liabilities. A $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078833" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossReclassifiedFromAccumulatedOciIntoIncomeEffectivePortionNet1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million gain,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c141078834" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossReclassifiedFromAccumulatedOciIntoIncomeEffectivePortionNet1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million gain and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078835" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-ForeignExchangeContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossReclassifiedFromAccumulatedOciIntoIncomeEffectivePortionNet1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.9</ix:nonFraction> million loss were reclassified from Accumulated other comprehensive loss to Cost of sales for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The estimated fair value amounts have been determined by the Company using the methods and assumptions described below. However, considerable judgment is required to interpret market data to develop estimates of fair value. Accordingly, the estimates presented herein are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the amounts the Company could realize in a current market exchange. The use of different market assumptions and/or estimation methodologies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have a material effect on the estimated fair value amounts.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Cash and Cash Equivalents</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Cash and cash equivalents are, by definition, short-term. Thus, the carrying amount is a reasonable estimate of fair value.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Accounts Receivable</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The fair value of accounts receivable approximates their carrying value due to their short-term nature.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Long-Term Debt</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Company's <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes bear interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c141078842" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>% per year. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the fair value approximated $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078843" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">313.8</ix:nonFraction> million, with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078844" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-Notes2032Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300.0</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">The Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes were retired at par on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 20, 2025. </em>As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the fair value of the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes approximated $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078847" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-SeniorSecuredNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">251.2</ix:nonFraction> million, with a carrying value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078848" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_DebtInstrumentAxis-SeniorSecuredNotesDue2026Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentCarryingAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">250.0</ix:nonFraction> million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">14,</em> &#8220;Notes Payable and Long-Term Debt&#8221;&#160;for further information regarding the Company&#8217;s long-term debt.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Foreign Currency</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s foreign currency contracts are based upon quoted market prices for similar instruments, thus leading to a Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> classification within the fair value hierarchy. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">5,</em> "Derivative Instruments", for further information regarding the Company's foreign currency contracts.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party warehouse in Tennessee used by the Company&#160;incurred significant tornado damage resulting in damage to the leaf tobacco. As a result, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078855" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_PublicUtilitiesInventoryAxis-LeafTobaccoInventoryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InventoryAdjustments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million inventory reserve related to its leaf tobacco inventory,&#160;which is included in Other operating income, net in the Consolidated Statement of Income for the&#160;year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023. </em>The leaf tobacco inventory is covered by the Company&#8217;s stock throughput insurance policy and the Company believes the inventory loss is probable of being fully recovered under the policy. As a result, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078856" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_PublicUtilitiesInventoryAxis-LeafTobaccoInventoryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InventoryAdjustments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">15.2</ix:nonFraction> million insurance recovery receivable which is included in Other current assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2022,</em> the Company determined that the incorrect weight had been used in calculating the amount of federal excise tax assessed and paid on its imported MYO cigar wraps during the years <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> - <em style="font: inherit;">2021.</em> As a result, the Company filed a refund claim for $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078860" contextRef="d_2022-01-01_2022-12-31_LitigationCaseAxis-RefundClaimWithTheAlcoholAndTobaccoTaxAndTradeBureauMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau for the overpayment of federal excise taxes, which was approved and paid in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em> This refund is presented in Other operating income, net on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Income for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023.</em></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company tests goodwill for impairment annually as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, </em>or more frequently when events or changes in circumstances indicate that the fair value is below its carrying value. The Company performed a qualitative assessment in evaluating its Zig-Zag and Stoker&#8217;s reporting units for impairment as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For the qualitative assessment,&#160;the Company considered macro and micro-economic indicators, changes in costs, overall financial performance and other relevant entity-specific events and noted <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> indications of impairment. The Company also considered the significant excess of fair values over carrying values as determined in the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;quantitative assessment.&#160;The underlying assumptions utilized during the <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> quantitative assessment remained sufficiently similar in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and in line with Company projections. Accordingly, such underlying assumptions on which the previous fair values were based had <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> sufficiently changed from <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>&#160;to suggest a material difference in the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;fair value assessments and thus indicated that the fair values of the reporting units as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;remained above their carrying amounts.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Company performed a quantitative assessment in evaluating its Zig-Zag and Stoker's reporting units.&#160; As part of that assessment, the Company used a discounted cash flow model&#160;(income approach) utilizing Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> unobservable inputs.&#160;The Company&#8217;s significant assumptions for the discount cash flow model include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, future cash flow projections, the weighted average cost of capital, the terminal growth rate, and the tax rate. The Company believes the current assumptions and estimates utilized in the discounted cash flow model are&#160;both reasonable and appropriate.&#160;The Company&#8217;s estimates of future cash flows are based on current regulatory and economic climates, recent operating results, and planned business strategies. These estimates could be negatively affected by changes in federal, state, or local regulations or economic downturns. Future cash flow estimates are, by their nature, subjective and actual results <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ materially from the Company&#8217;s estimates. If the Company&#8217;s ongoing estimates of future cash flows are <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141078878">not</span> met or if discount rates change, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have to record impairment charges in future periods. Based on the analysis performed, the Company concluded that <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impairment exists for its Zig-Zag or Stoker's reporting units as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company performed a qualitative assessment of its indefinite-lived intangible assets. As part of this assessment, the Company evaluated whether indicators of impairment were present by considering macro and micro-economic factors, along with market and other relevant company-specific events and determined that there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> indications of impairment as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> the Company performed a quantitative assessment of its indefinite-lived&#160;intangible assets and noted <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> indicators of impairment as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024.&#160;</em>The Company&#8217;s fair value methodology for the quantitative assessment is primarily based on the relief from royalty approach. Significant assumptions in this approach include, but are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, projected revenue, the weighted average cost of capital and royalty rate.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i>Non-Marketable Equity Investments and Option Agreements</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company records its non-marketable equity investments without a readily determinable fair value, that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accounted for under the equity method, at cost, with adjustments for impairment and observable price changes.&#160;Should assumptions underlying the determination of the fair values of the Company&#8217;s non-marketable equity and debt security investments change, it could result in material future impairment charges.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Captive Investments - Available-for-Sale Marketable Securities</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the Company formed a captive insurance company, Interchange, IC, incorporated in the District of Columbia, to write a portion of its insurance coverage, including with respect to general product, and officer and director liability coverages under deductible reinsurance policies. Interchange, IC is a fully licensed captive insurance company holding a certificate of authority from the District of Columbia Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking. Interchange, IC is consolidated in the Company&#8217;s financial statements. During <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> Interchange IC received approval from the District of Columbia Department of Insurance, Securities and Banking to operate as a group captive. On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 14, 2025, </em>a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investor subscribed $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078977" contextRef="d_2025-07-14_2025-07-14_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationLessThanWhollyOwnedSubsidiaryParentOwnershipInterestChangesSaleOfInterestByParent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">11.0</ix:nonFraction> million for an interest in Interchange IC&#8217;s parent company, which contributed the investment to Interchange IC. Insurance reserves were $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078978" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SelfInsuranceReserve" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078979" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_ScheduleOfEquityMethodInvestmentEquityMethodInvesteeNameAxis-CanadianAmericanStandardHempMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SelfInsuranceReserve" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction> for <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024,</em> respectively. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> policy has been underwritten for the benefit of the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party investor. The group captive will write policies for both companies. The Company will continue to control and consolidate the entity.</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The investments held within the captive are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available for operating activities and are carried at fair value on the consolidated balance sheet. They consist of money market, stocks, corporate bonds, government securities and real estate investment trusts. The Company believes any investments held with gross unrealized losses to be temporary and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the result of credit risk.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 19, 2025, </em>the Company entered into an indenture relating to the issuance and sale of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078989" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300.0</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate principal amount of its <ix:nonFraction id="c141078990" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>% Senior Secured Notes due <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2032</em> Notes&#8221;), by and among the Company, the guarantors party thereto and GLAS Trust Company LLC, as trustee and notes collateral agent. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes incur interest at a rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c141078994" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">7.625</ix:nonFraction>%, payable semi-annually in arrears on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 15 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15 </em>of each year, commencing on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 15, 2025. </em>Proceeds from the offering were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141078995" contextRef="d_2025-02-19_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfLongTermDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">293.0</ix:nonFraction> million and were used to redeem the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes (as defined below) and for general corporate purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes are fully and unconditionally guaranteed on a senior secured basis, jointly and severally, by certain existing and future wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries of the Company (collectively, the &#8220;Guarantors&#8221; as defined in the indenture governing the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes or the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2032</em> Notes Indenture&#8221;). The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes and the related guarantees are secured by <em style="font: inherit;">first</em>-priority liens on substantially all of the existing and future assets of the Company and the Guarantors that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> secure the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility (as defined below), subject to certain exceptions. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture contains covenants that, among other things, restrict the ability of the Company and its restricted subsidiaries to: (i) grant or incur liens; (ii) incur, assume or guarantee additional indebtedness; (iii) sell or otherwise dispose of assets, including capital stock of subsidiaries; (iv) make certain investments; (v) pay dividends, make distributions or redeem or repurchase capital stock; (vi) engage in certain transactions with affiliates; and (vii) consolidate or merge with or into, or sell substantially all of our assets to another entity. These covenants are subject to several limitations and exceptions set forth in the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture. For instance, the Company is generally permitted to make restricted payments, including the payment of dividends to shareholders, provided that, at the time of payment, or as a result of payment, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> in default on its covenants; however, there are earnings and market capitalization requirements that if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met could limit the aggregate amount of quarterly dividends payable during a fiscal year. The <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes Indenture provides for customary events of default. The Company was compliance with all covenants under the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company incurred debt issuance costs attributable to the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079011" contextRef="i_2025-02-19_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2032SeniorSecuredNotesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredFinanceCostsGross" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million which are amortized to interest expense using the straight-line method over the expected life of the <em style="font: inherit;">2032</em> Notes.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><i><em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 11, 2021, </em>the Company closed a private offering ("the Offering") of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079015" contextRef="i_2021-02-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-SeniorSecuredNotes2026Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">250.0</ix:nonFraction> million aggregate principal amount of its <ix:nonFraction id="c141079016" contextRef="i_2021-02-11_DebtInstrumentAxis-SeniorSecuredNotes2026Member" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">5.625</ix:nonFraction>% senior secured notes due <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2026</em> Notes&#8221;). The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes incurred interest at a rate of <em style="font: inherit;">5.625%,</em> payable semi-annually in arrears on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 15 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> August 15 </em>of each year, commencing on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 15, 2021. </em>The Company used the proceeds from the offering (i) to repay all obligations under and terminate the <em style="font: inherit;">2018</em> First Lien Credit Facility, (ii) to pay related fees, costs and expenses and (iii) for general corporate purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

The <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes and the related guarantees were secured by <em style="font: inherit;">first</em>-priority liens on substantially all of the assets of the Company and the Guarantors, subject to certain exceptions.&#160;</p>

Upon redemption of the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes, the indenture governing the <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> Notes was satisfied and discharged in accordance with its terms.</p>

Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility, the ABL Borrower <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>draw up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079054" contextRef="i_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million under revolving credit loans and last-in, last-out (&#8220;LILO&#8221;) loans. plus (b)&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079070">85%</span> of the face value of all eligible accounts of the ABL Borrower minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.&#160; The <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> ABL Facility also includes a LILO borrowing base equal to the sum of (a) the lesser of: (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141079073" contextRef="d_2023-11-07_2023-11-07_DebtInstrumentAxis-AssetBackedRevolvingCreditFacility2023Member" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DebtInstrumentPercentageUsedInCalculationOfLiloBorrowingBase" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">10</ix:nonFraction>% of the lower of (A) the market value (on a <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> in <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> out basis) of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory of the ABL Borrower and (B) the cost of the sum of eligible inventory, plus eligible in-transit inventory and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079077">10%</span> of the NOLV percentage of the lower of&#160; (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(A) or (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)(B); plus (b)&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079080">10%</span> of the face amount of eligible account; minus (c) the amount of all eligible reserves.</p>

provided that such <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079099">$9.4</span>&#160;million level shall automatically increase in proportion to the amount of any increase in the aggregate revolving credit commitments thereunder in connection with any incremental facility.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">25</em> prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for the financial statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax return. For those benefits to be recognized, a tax position must be more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be sustained upon examination by taxing authorities. The amount recognized is measured as the largest amount of benefit that is greater than <em style="font: inherit;">50</em> percent likely of being realized upon ultimate settlement. The Company has determined that they did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079147">not</span> have any uncertain tax positions requiring recognition as a result of the provisions of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">25.</em> The Company&#8217;s policy is to recognize interest and penalties accrued on uncertain tax positions as part of interest expense. For the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> estimated interest or penalties were recognized for the uncertainty of tax positions taken. The Company files income tax returns in the U.S. federal jurisdiction and various state jurisdictions. In general, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer subject to U.S. federal and state tax examinations for years prior to <em style="font: inherit;">2022.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em> the U.S. government enacted the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Security Act (the &#8220;CARES Act&#8221;) to provide certain relief as a result of the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> Pandemic. The CARES Act provides tax relief, along with other stimulus measures, including a provision for an Employee Retention Credit (&#8220;ERC&#8221;). ERC is a refundable tax credit for employers who kept employees on their payroll during the COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> Pandemic. The Company applied for the ERC in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company considered the ERC to be a contingent gain. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company received and recorded an employee retention credit totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079160" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_IncomeStatementLocationAxis-OtherIncomeNetMember" unitRef="USD" name="tpb:GainFromEmployeRetentionTaxCredit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.5</ix:nonFraction> million, within the &#8220;Other income, net&#8221; in our Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">16.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) Retirement Savings Plan</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company sponsors a voluntary <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) retirement savings plan. Eligible employees <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to contribute up to <ix:nonFraction id="c141079178" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">15</ix:nonFraction>% of their annual earnings subject to certain limitations. For the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> plan years, the Company contributed <ix:nonFraction id="c141079182" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerContributionPercentageForEmployeeContributingFourPercentOrGreater" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>% to employees who contributed <ix:nonFraction id="c141079183" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>% or more of their annual earnings. Employees contributing less than <ix:nonFraction id="c141079184" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerContributionPercentageForEmployeeContributingLessThanFourPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">4</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;received a <ix:nonFraction id="c141079185" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercentOfMatch" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% match on their contributions. Additionally, for all years presented, the Company made discretionary contributions of <ix:nonFraction id="c141079186" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="tpb:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerDiscretionaryContributionPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">1</ix:nonFraction>% to all employees, regardless of an employee&#8217;s contribution level. Company contributions to this plan were approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079187" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;for <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079189" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079191" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">17.</em> Lease Commitments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s leases consist primarily of leased property for manufacturing, warehouse, corporate offices and retail space as well as vehicle leases.&#160;At lease inception, the Company recognizes a lease right of use asset and lease liability calculated as the present value of future minimum lease payments.&#160;Some leases <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of other components such as taxes, insurance, maintenance and operating expenses. When payments related to these other components are considered fixed, they are included in the determination of the lease liability due to the Company&#8217;s election to combine lease and non-lease components and account for them as a single lease component. Otherwise, they are recognized as variable payments, along with variable payments <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> based on a rate or index, in the period in which the obligation for those payments is incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">In general, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recognize renewal periods within the lease terms as there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant barriers to ending the lease at the initial term. Leases with an initial term of <em style="font: inherit;">12</em> months or less are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded on the balance sheet. Lease expense for these leases is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The components of lease expense consist of the following:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Nearly all the lease contracts for the Company do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provide a readily determinable implicit rate. For these contracts, the Company uses a discount rate that approximates its incremental borrowing rate at the time of the lease commencement.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">18.</em> Share Incentive Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 22, 2021, </em>the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors adopted the Turning Point Brands, Inc. <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Equity Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2021</em> Plan&#8221;), pursuant to which awards <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be granted to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants. In addition, the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan provides for the granting of nonqualified stock options to employees of the Company or any subsidiary of the Company. Pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan, <ix:nonFraction id="c141079208" contextRef="i_2021-03-22_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,290,000</ix:nonFraction> shares, plus <ix:nonFraction id="c141079209" contextRef="i_2021-03-22_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2015EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100,052</ix:nonFraction> shares remaining available for issuance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Equity Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2015</em> Plan&#8221;), of TPB Common Stock are reserved for issuance as awards to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants as compensation for past or future services or the attainment of certain performance goals. The <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan is scheduled to terminate on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 21, 2031. </em>The <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan is administered by the compensation committee (the &#8220;Committee&#8221;) of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors. The Committee determines the vesting criteria for the awards, with such criteria to be specified in the award agreement. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, net of forfeitures, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c141079214" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">437,024</ix:nonFraction> Restricted Stock Units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;), <ix:nonFraction id="c141079215" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">122,570</ix:nonFraction> options and <ix:nonFraction id="c141079216" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardsGrantedNetOfForfeituresNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">94,421</ix:nonFraction> Performance Based Restricted Stock Units (&#8220;PRSUs&#8221;) granted under the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan. There are <ix:nonFraction id="c141079218" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2021EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">736,037</ix:nonFraction> shares available for future grant under the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April 28, 2016, </em>the Board of Directors of the Company adopted the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan, pursuant to which awards could have been granted to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants. In addition, the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan provided for the granting of nonqualified stock options to employees of the Company or any subsidiary of the Company. Upon adoption of the <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plan, the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan was terminated, and the Company determined <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> additional grants would be made under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan. However, all awards issued under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been previously terminated or forfeited remain outstanding and continue unaffected. There are <ix:nonFraction id="c141079228" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-TurningPointBrandsInc2015EquityIncentivePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> shares available for grant under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">Under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plans, the total intrinsic value of options exercised during the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079236" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.9</ix:nonFraction> million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079237" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079238" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardOptionsExercisesInPeriodTotalIntrinsicValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, under the <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2021</em> Plans,&#160;the risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Treasury rate for the expected life at the time of grant. The expected volatility is based on the average long-term historical volatilities of peer companies. We intend to continue to consistently use the same group of publicly traded peer companies to determine expected volatility until sufficient information regarding volatility of our share price becomes available or until the selected companies are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer suitable for this purpose. Due to our limited trading history, we are using the simplified method presented by SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">107</em> to calculate expected holding periods, which represent the periods of time for which options granted are expected to be outstanding. We will continue to use this method until we have sufficient historical exercise experience to give us confidence in the reliability of our calculations. The fair values of these options were determined using the Black-Scholes option pricing model.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">The Company has recorded compensation expense related to the options based on the provisions of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">718</em> under which the fixed portion of such expense is determined as the fair value of the options on the date of grant and amortized over the vesting period. The Company recorded compensation expense related to the options of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079248" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction> million , $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079249" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079250" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million for the years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively.&#160;At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the options have been fully expensed with <ix:nonFraction id="c141079253" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-EmployeeStockOptionMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">zero</ix:nonFraction> remaining.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">PRSUs are restricted stock units subject to both performance-based and service-based vesting conditions. The number of shares of TPB Common Stock a recipient will receive upon vesting of a PRSU is calculated by reference to certain performance metrics related to the Company&#8217;s performance over a&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141079254">five</span>-year&#160;period. PRSUs will vest on the measurement date, which is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> more than&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" name="tpb:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPeriodBetweenPerformancePeriodAndMeasurementDate" id="c141079256" format="ixt-sec:duryear">65</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;days after the performance period provided the applicable service and performance conditions are satisfied. At <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c141079257" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">273,098</ix:nonFraction> PRSUs outstanding.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">19.</em> Contingencies </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 9, 2020, </em>a purported stockholder of Turning Point Brands, Inc., Paul-Emile Berteau, filed a complaint in the Delaware Court of Chancery relating to the merger of Standard Diversified, Inc. (&#8220;SDI&#8221;) with a TPB subsidiary (&#8220;Merger Sub&#8221;) pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization, dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> April 7, 2020, </em>by and among TPB, SDI and Merger Sub.&#160;The parties attended a mediation in late <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022 </em>where a settlement was reached. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 12, 2023, </em>the Court approved the settlement and dismissed the action with prejudice. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023, </em>the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c141079277" contextRef="i_2023-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherCurrentAssetsMember_GainContingenciesByNatureAxis-PositiveOutcomeOfLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyReceivableCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">4.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million receivable in other current assets, and a corresponding gain on settlement in other income on its Consolidated Statement of Income for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023. </em>These funds were received in <em style="font: inherit;"> January 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">Other major tobacco companies are defendants in product liability claims. In a number of these cases, the amounts of punitive and compensatory damages sought are significant and, if such a claim were brought against the Company, could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-align: justify;">The probable losses, if any, associated with any such lawsuits are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently reasonably estimable and therefore are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> accrued.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
